reachable: YES, reachable at the scored read position and gradient-carrying after step 0. (a) Scored position: cups_probe.py:124-125 puts the read command alone at position 2r and _fwd_pred reads pred at rpos=2r (line 139) -- a command position, which is exactly where the new channel adds `contrib` (arch file:163). At that step obs_live=0 so no write/erase fires, but s_r is read BEFORE any step-r write (line 79-80), over a store built from steps 0..r-1, which is the identical computation the read path performs during training -- so there is no train/score regime mismatch on the read (in training collate keeps cmd+obs valid together, so live=1 everywhere, but that only affects the step's own write, which never feeds its own read). (b) Causality verified by execution (scratchpad/t4.py) with tp_out randomized to make the channel live (max |contrib| 3.23): perturbing obs_j by N(0,3) moves cmd predictions only at i>j, "VIOLATION at cmd none" for every j. (c) Gradient (scratchpad/t6.py, 3 AdamW steps on a cmd-position MSE): at step 0 ONLY tp_out.weight (4.6e-4) and tp_out.bias (7.0e-4) receive gradient; addr_src, addr_dst, addr_in, ptr_q, ptr_k, tp_move_gate, tp_alpha, tp_gate are all exactly 0.0 -- the zero-init bottleneck the author names as a risk (lines 101-104). From step 1 on every one of them is non-zero (addr_src 8.6e-5 -> 2.1e-4, ptr_q 5.4e-6 -> 1.6e-4, tp_gate 3.1e-2 -> 4.2e-2), so the channel is not structurally dead, only slow to start. (d) The head (r18_transition_forwardmodel_consistency) does not re-point forward, and harness._train computes the loss from pred_full at cmd positions (harness.py:88-93), so contrib is in the loss path. (e) Optim routing claims (lines 117-120) are exactly right, verified by running the genome's optim (scratchpad/t5.py): MUON gets addr_dst.weight and addr_src.weight (64,256 identical-shape pair) alongside the inherited r18/r22 addressing pairs; SPECTRAL CAP gets tp_out.weight together with tr_read.weight and x_out.weight; ptr_q/ptr_k (64,768) are excluded by the `shape[1] != D` clause and stay on AdamW.
summary:
The code does what the hypothesis says the mechanism does. I checked the recurrence against a from-scratch reference implementation of the formula as written and it matches to 3.7e-8; a hand-constructed two-hop chain (expose A -> mv A->C -> mv C->E -> read E) with orthogonal addresses returns the exposed content at E with cosine 1.0000 and relative norm 0.999 to the right content, 0.032 to the distractor, and leaves 0.001 relative norm at the erased source -- so "take what is at A and put it at B", plus the delta-rule overwrite claim, is real and not decorative. Addresses come from the raw command embedding only, s_i is read before the step-i write, the pointer mask is strictly j<i and pad-aware, the channel touches only pred[:,0::2] and returns h untouched, and full-forward causality holds under perturbation with the channel forced live. The trunk-geometry claim is exact: d=192, ffn hidden 768 = 4*d, heads 4, layers 4, matching realenv SeqWorldModel's defaults (the crossover partner). The optim-routing claims are exact, including the non-obvious one that ptr_q/ptr_k escape the Muon sibling rule.

Two of the three data claims the design rests on I confirmed against the real frozen embeddings rather than the jail sample: mv-step observation embeddings deviate from their mean by at most 4.8e-7 across 4000 mv steps (they are one constant vector), and the expose observation and the later read observation are bit-identical (|diff|max exactly 0.0 over 490 matched pairs). The claim about the parents is also accurate: r18's _transition_reads uses one address per step for both read and write (r18 file:250,258,271), and its file memory writes obs_tok at a key derived from the same command (r18:327,333).

I also retired the author's stated single largest risk, which they said they could not check from the jail. Using the real val/train embedding caches (disjoint images) I trained EXACTLY the module shape they wrote -- LayerNorm(768) -> Linear(768,256) -> GELU -> two unnormalized-then-unit 64-d heads -- on the two consistency constraints the mechanism actually needs, and on HELD-OUT images a_src("mv A B") picks a_dst("cat A") over in-window foils 95.3% of the time and a_dst("mv A B") picks a_src("cat B") 99.6% of the time (chance ~12.5%), with mean cos(a_src(x), a_dst(x)) = 0.49 on mv commands, i.e. the two heads do not collapse. The pooled encoder does keep source and destination separable; that risk is not what will sink this candidate.

The only real mismatch is bookkeeping: "bit-identical to the parent at initialization" is false against the actual parent genome, which runs r22 at d=176/ffn 2x. The child is +48% parameters (859k of that pure trunk widening, before the 922k of new channel) and +66% CPU train-step time (320ms -> 532ms at B=32,L=33; forward 33.4ms -> 45.9ms at matched geometry). The author discloses the trunk change as a confound in the body, so nothing is concealed, but a child-vs-parent delta on this slot measures the channel AND the trunk together and must not be reported as measuring the channel.

divergences.claim: "Zero-init tp_out makes the forward bit-identical to the parent at initialization." (hypothesis.txt:115; and the shipped DESCRIPTION, arch file line 23: "so the forward is bit-identical to r22 at init")
divergences.what_the_code_does: The child is bit-identical to r22 ONLY when r22 is built at the child's trunk hyperparameters (d=192, ffn_mult=4). The actual parent genome (BRIEF.md:33, arch r22_prefix_content_xattention with no params) uses r22's defaults d=176, ffn_mult=2, so the child is a different network at init: 3,687,992 -> 5,468,483 params (+48%), of which 921,803 are the new channel and 858,688 are pure trunk widening. The hypothesis body does disclose the trunk change and calls it "a real confound" (lines 71-73, 105-107), so this is a self-contradicting sentence in the cost notes rather than a hidden claim -- but as written the sentence is false, and it is the sentence a later reader will use to decide whether a child-vs-parent delta isolates the new channel. It does not.

divergences.claim: "...enters the command-position prediction through a zero-init (D,D) readout under a sigmoid gate fed the RMS of the retrieved value, the RMS of the copy, and the peak attention mass" (hypothesis.txt:65-66); likewise "A learned alpha blends the copy with the raw retrieved value" (line 65).
divergences.what_the_code_does: Both tp_gate and tp_alpha are fed `gi = cat([h_cmd, feat])` -- the trunk hidden state at the command position IN ADDITION to the three retrieval statistics. So the gate and the blend are not pure functions of retrieval quality; they can key on the trunk state (i.e. on position/what-is-being-asked) independently of whether anything was actually retrieved. Understatement, not overstatement, and it does not create a leak (h_cmd is causal), but the description omits the dominant input.
divergences.evidence: arch__r23_dual_address_transport_pointer.py:153-158 (`feat = cat([rms_read, rms_copy, sharp]); gi = cat([h_cmd, feat])`), constructors at lines 62-65 are `nn.Linear(self.d + 3, 1)`.

divergences.claim: The recurrence as written in hypothesis.txt:46-47: `mem <- tp_decay*mem + a_dst (beta_i (v_i - a_dst^T mem))^T - a_src (g_erase[i] g_move[i] s_i)^T`.
divergences.what_the_code_does: The erase term additionally carries the `live` factor: `w_erase = -(g_erase * g_move * live) * s_i` (line 91), and beta_i is `g_write * live` (line 90), which the hypothesis only implies by naming beta_i. The code's version is the safer one -- no erase and no write at a padded step or at the final read step, where the observation is withheld -- and it is what you want. Recorded only because the transcribed formula is not literally what runs.
